mission.title: Places in Town and Giving Directions

theory.title: Places in town and asking for directions
theory.explanation: Ask politely for directions with Excuse me, how do I get to ...? Give instructions with imperatives such as go straight on, turn left and cross the road. Describe locations with next to, opposite, between and behind. Use can/can't for simple possibilities and restrictions.
theory.tip: Use the imperative without a subject: Turn left, not You turn left. Say on the left/right and at the traffic lights.

patterns.label: Block 1 · Asking the way
patterns.pattern: Excuse me, how do I get to ...?
examples: Excuse me, how do I get to the library?
Can you tell me the way to the station?

patterns.label: Block 2 · Giving directions
examples: Go straight on for two minutes.
Turn right at the traffic lights.

patterns.label: Block 3 · Place prepositions
examples: The bank is next to the post office.
The museum is opposite the park.

patterns.label: Block 4 · At the corner
patterns.pattern: on the corner; at the end of
examples: The café is on the corner.
The school is at the end of this street.

patterns.label: Block 5 · Imperatives
examples: Cross the road carefully.
Take the first street on the left.

patterns.label: Block 6 · Distance
patterns.pattern: It's near/far; about five minutes away
examples: The station is near the square.
It's about ten minutes away on foot.

patterns.label: Block 7 · Can for directions
examples: You can take the bus to the museum.
You can't park here.

patterns.label: Block 8 · Transport questions
examples: Is there a bus stop near here?
Where is the nearest train station?

patterns.label: Block 9 · Sequencing directions
examples: First, go straight on. Then turn left.
Finally, cross the bridge.

patterns.label: Block 10 · Checking understanding
examples: So, I go past the bank and turn right?
Is it far from here?

content.passage: Hi Sam,\nI'm at the train station. To get to the museum, go straight on along King Street. Turn left at the traffic lights and cross the bridge. The museum is on your right, opposite the library. The café is next to the museum, so we can meet there at three. It takes about eight minutes on foot. See you soon,\nAlex

content.audioTranscript: Hello. Can you tell me the way to the library? Certainly. Go straight on along Park Road. Turn left at the traffic lights and cross the bridge. The library is opposite the museum, next to the post office. Is it far? No, it's about five minutes on foot. Is there a bus stop near the library? Yes, there is one on the corner. Thank you very much. You're welcome.
